# Draft:Key events of the 21st century

The world at the beginning of the century was marked with unprecedented technological advancement, the rise of the Internet, and social crises such as the September 11 attacks and the COVID-19 pandemic.
September 11 attacks and the Middle East (2001-2021)
In 2001, Osama bin Laden had led the Islamic militant organization al-Qaeda for years, committing terrorist attacks against the United States and its assets in various countries. He had opposed American foreign policy and its presence in Israel. These motivations led bin Laden to declare war  against the United States in 1996.
These plans to attack America culminated on September 11, 2001 in a series of terrorist attacks called the September 11 attacks. In the early morning of that day, nineteen hijackers affiliated with al-Qaeda hijacked four commercial airplanes. These planes were deliberately crashed into targets across the Northeastern United States. American Airlines Flight 11 was piloted into the North Tower of the World Trade Center in New York City by ringleader Mohammed Atta. The crash killed all 92 passengers on board and approximately 1,600 people in the building. It was the deadliest plane crash of all time. United Airlines Flight 175 was piloted into the South Tower, killing all 65 people on board and approximately 900 in the building. Cumulatively, 2,763 people died in these two attacks, mostly when the two 110-story buildings collapsed.
American Airlines Flight 77 was hijacked and flown into one side of the the Pentagon, killing 189 people. United Airlines Flight 93 was the fourth hijacked plane. Although it is unknown what the true target of the terrorists was, there is high probability that it would have been the United States Capitol building in Washington, D. C..  After the plane was hijacked, the passengers on board fought back against the terrorists; during a struggle for the plane, it crashed in a field in Stonycreek Township in Pennsylvania, ending the lives of all 44 people on board. The passengers of Flight 93 saved the lives of many people on the ground, and are now acclaimed as heroes.
The attacks quickly became the deadliest terrorist attack in human history. 2,996 people were killed, including the 19 hijackers, and the 2,977 victims who were going about their daily lives; thousands more were injured.
Government response of the United States
The response of the United States government was swift. That evening, the Central Intelligence Agency gained sufficient information to identify that the attacks were masterminded by Islamic terrorist group al-Qaeda under Osama bin Laden. President George W. Bush was informed of this, and days later he announced the initiation of the war on terror to strike back against those who had caused the attacks.
War on terror
The war on terror officially began on September 14, 2001, when the Authorization for Use of Military Force of 2001 was passed in the United States, giving the president the authority to use force against those who had organized the attacks. The NATO coalition’s primary target was Afghanistan’s Taliban government for harboring al-Qaeda. An invasion began of the country on October 7, 2001 with the assistance of the Northern Alliance, who had been fighting in a lurid civil war against the Taliban. The invasion was complete by December, but the war lasted 20 more years until ending with the 2021 Taliban offensive and victory. Meanwhile, the mission to retrieve Osama bin Laden during the invasion had failed, as he evaded capture during the Battle of Tora Bora and escaped to Pakistan. After a ten-year manhunt, bin Laden was located in 2011 hiding in a compound in Abbottabad, Pakistan; Operation Neptune Spear led to his killing by American forces.
Despite the carnage of the Afghanistan war, the war on terror would continue with more military campaigns. In 2002, George W. Bush and British Prime Minister Tony Blair set their sights on the nearby country of Iraq. They aimed to disarm the country of their alleged weapons of mass destruction (allegations that were denied by a United Nations inspection team) and supported loose allegations that Saddam Hussein, the president of Iraq, and al-Qaeda were linked. Nevertheless, a United States-led combination of forces invaded Iraq in 2003. During the invasion, Hussein was captured and later tried and executed.
The Iraq War continued from 2003 until 2011 when  American forces withdrew from the country.
The war on terror resulted in 4.6 million deaths and 38 million people displaced.

In the early 2010s, an influx of uprisings across the Arab World occurred with a common goal of installing democracies in these countries. Across the region, many rulers were deposed violently - or attempts were made to depose them, resulting in civil wars.
Rise of the Islamic State
positions during the Battle of Mosul (2016–2017).]]
The Syrian civil war allowed for a new terrorist organization to come about in the mid-2010s: the Islamic State. At the apex of its territorial control in 2015, it governed over half of Syria and a third of Iraq. The June 2014 northern Iraq offensive led to the initiation of a coalition war against the Islamic State to halt their efforts. By the late 2010s, the Islamic State had lost so much territory from the war that they regressed back to carrying out insurgency.
Because of the Islamic State, terrorism was more open and pronounced than it had ever been in history in the 2010s. Attacks were commonplace throughout the world and resulted in thousands of deaths and injuries.
Rest of the world (2000-2019)
The early 20th century global scheme was influenced by a world economy and a new wave of globalization with rapid technological progress that heralded the increasing popularity of the Internet and the inception of the smartphone. The Internet became a complex depository of information that was accessible to anyone, especially with the coming about of social media. Internet technology also enabled sustained amelioration in the complexity of artificial intelligence.
Centered in the United States, the 2008 financial crisis triggered the Great Recession, a period of decline in worldwide economies.
Climate change
indirectly caused by global warming, 2020.]]
Caused by human activity, climate change has caused unprecedented emergency to the condition of Earth. Carbon dioxide has increased during the century, threatening every species on the planet. The effects became widespread in the early 21st century: desertification, commonality of heat waves and wildfires, the retreat of glaciers, increased tropical cyclone intensity; global warming has emerged as the greatest global threat to all life in the 21st century.
Global crisis (2020-present)
, 2020.]]
In 2020, the virus strain SARS-CoV-2 caused an outbreak of the coronavirus disease. Its societal impacts were numerous: lockdowns were imposed, which contributed to economic stagnation. The death toll from the pandemic could be as high as 33 million, and it is widely considered to be in the top five deadliest pandemics. Modern medical advancements and superior hygiene prevented the pandemic from being any deadlier than it was, and the pandemic was over by 2023.
Increase in deadly wars (2020-present)
, 2023.]]
The 2020s have been the deadliest decade for war of the century. Contributing factors are the Russo-Ukrainian war; and the Gaza war that is ongoing since 2023.
